sentence.text: European cement is cutting its emissions.

why_it_matters.text: Cement made this way costs more than the cement it replaces, so whether Europe gets it depends on who covers the difference.

facts.label: Routes
facts.text: Four routes are being built: post-combustion carbon capture (15 projects), oxyfuel carbon capture (6), alternative fuels in the kiln (1) and direct separation carbon capture (1).

parts.list: post-combustion carbon capture (15 projects), oxyfuel carbon capture (6), alternative fuels in the kiln (1) and direct separation carbon capture (1)

facts.label: The gap
facts.text: Low-carbon cement costs 75-150% above a conventional plant to make, on the International Energy Agency's figures.

parts.name: Production cost premium of near-zero emissions cement using CCS

sourced: Production cost premium of near-zero emissions cement using CCS

facts.label: Pipeline
facts.text: 33 European cement projects are under way, 5 of them have taken a final investment decision, and 1 is paused.

facts.label: Decisive exposure
facts.text: Importers of cement pay for the carbon in what they bring into Europe, currently €75.46 per tonne.

facts.label: Binding constraint
facts.text: Green premium against willingness to pay — a market constraint, acted on by 4 ranked measures at 3 of combined weight.
